name: South Korea
note: A doctor's certificate is attached to the death report (사망신고), which cohabiting relatives must file at a city, eup or myeon office within one month of learning of the death. The report closes the person's record in the national electronic family-relations register and replaces any resident-registration report, so the resident registration is cancelled; the National Pension Service and the NHIS draw on these data. At the same desk heirs can file one request (안심상속 원스톱 서비스) that queries financial institutions via the Financial Supervisory Service, taxes, social insurance, pensions, vehicles and land, which is the main official route by which the private sector is reached.

steps.title: Examining doctor issues the medical or post-mortem certificate
steps.who: A doctor (or dentist/Korean-medicine doctor) who personally examined the patient or the body; post-mortem certificates also by state forensic doctors.
steps.summary: Only a doctor who directly examined the patient or the body may issue a death diagnosis certificate (사망진단서) or post-mortem certificate (시체검안서), given to the family or, for post-mortem certificates, to the prosecutor conducting an inquest.

steps.title: Prosecutor (or police on delegation) conducts an inquest
steps.who: The district public prosecutor; may delegate to judicial police officers.
steps.trigger: An unnatural or suspected unnatural death.
steps.summary: Korea has no coroner; the prosecutor must conduct an inquest (검시) of unnatural deaths and may order the post-mortem examination.

steps.title: Report the death to the city/eup/myeon head
steps.who: Cohabiting relatives must report; other relatives, cohabitants, the manager of the place of death, or the local dong/tong/ri head may report.

deadline.text: within one month of learning of the death

steps.summary: The death report (사망신고) with the medical or post-mortem certificate is filed at the office for the deceased's registration base, the informant's address or present location, or the place of death, burial or cremation. Late reporting carries an administrative fine of up to ₩50,000, and the office must send reminders.

steps.title: Officials report disaster, unclaimed and unidentified deaths
steps.who: The investigating authority (disasters), prison governors, mayors handling deaths without kin, police officers (unidentified bodies).
steps.trigger: Death in a disaster, in prison, of a person without kin, or of an unidentified person.
steps.summary: Where no family reports, the state does: authorities report disaster deaths, mayors report deaths of persons without kin they have buried, and police report unidentified bodies with the inquest record.

steps.title: Report the cremation (or burial) to the local mayor
steps.who: The person arranging the cremation (before it) or burial (within 30 days after).
steps.summary: Burial or cremation may not take place within 24 hours of death; a cremation must be reported in advance to the mayor responsible for the crematorium and a burial within 30 days. The statute does not make the cremation report depend on the death report having been filed.

steps.title: Register closed; certificates issued on request
steps.who: The person, spouse and lineal blood relatives; others only for state duties, litigation, other statutory requirements or a legitimate interest set by Supreme Court rules.
steps.summary: On death the individual family-relations register is closed (폐쇄등록부). The death appears on the Basic Certificate (기본증명서) and other registration certificates, which are restricted to the family and to listed requesters.

steps.title: Death entered in the central electronic family register
steps.who: The city/eup/myeon head, on the electronic system kept by the Minister of National Court Administration.
steps.latencyNote: 신고서류 등을 수리한 때에는 … 즉시 등록부에 기록 (fam-rule-45)
steps.summary: Registration work is processed on the national electronic system and the registers, including closed ones, are held by the National Court Administration.

steps.title: Resident registration cancelled without a separate report
steps.who: The office that accepted the death report, notifying the mayor/county head/ward head of the place of resident registration.
steps.summary: A death report under the family-registration Act stands in for any resident-registration report: the registration office notifies the place of resident registration, which must cancel (말소) the resident registration.

steps.title: National Pension Service uses the family-registration data
steps.who: The National Pension Service, through shared use of family-registration electronic data under the E-Government Act.
steps.latencyNote: 전산정보자료를 공동이용할 수 있다; no time set (pension-123-2)
steps.summary: The NPS may use the family-registration data directly, and the family's separate duty to report a pensioner's death within one month is waived if the death report was filed within that month.

steps.title: Family reports a pensioner's death where the death report was late
steps.who: The persons obliged to report the death under art. 85 of the family-registration Act.
steps.trigger: Death of a pension recipient, where no death report was filed within one month.

deadline.text: within one month of learning of the death

steps.summary: Only where the death report itself was not made within one month must the family separately report the death to the National Pension Service.

steps.title: Health insurance status ends; NHIS obtains registration data
steps.who: The National Health Insurance Service, by requesting resident and family-registration data.
steps.summary: Insured status ends on the day after death, and the NHIS may require resident-registration and family-registration data to manage eligibility.

steps.title: Heirs apply for the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service
steps.who: First-order heirs and spouse (then second- and third-order heirs, substitutionary heirs, estate administrators), at the family-registration desk or online.
steps.trigger: Filing of the death report, or within one year after the end of the month of death.

deadline.text: with the death report or within one year from the end of the month of death

steps.summary: The family-registration official who takes the death report also takes the application for the 안심상속 원스톱 서비스, which queries the deceased's financial accounts, tax, social insurance, pensions, vehicles, land and buildings in one request.

steps.title: Financial institutions queried through the Financial Supervisory Service
steps.who: The receiving office forwards the request; the Financial Supervisory Service collects results from financial institutions.
steps.trigger: An application under the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service.
steps.summary: The heir's single application is passed to the FSS, which queries financial institutions and posts the results on its website; tax, social insurance and pension results are posted by the NTS, NHIS and NPS within the same period. This is the only official route found by which banks are told of a death, and it depends on the heirs applying.

steps.title: Tax and other public bodies queried in the same request
steps.who: The receiving office; the National Tax Service, local tax officials, vehicle, building and land systems.
steps.trigger: An application under the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service.

deadline.text: within 20 working days (local tax, vehicles and buildings within 7)

steps.summary: The same request triggers searches of national tax arrears and refunds, local tax, vehicle ownership, building and land records, with results given to the applicant.

steps.title: Heirs file an inheritance tax return
steps.who: Heirs or legatees liable to inheritance tax.

deadline.text: within 6 months from the end of the month in which succession opened

steps.summary: Inheritance tax must be reported to the competent tax office within six months from the end of the month of death.

steps.title: Heirs accept or renounce at the family court
steps.summary: Heirs may make a simple or qualified acceptance or renounce within three months of learning of the succession, extendable by the family court.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: One month from learning of the death.

informantDuty.note: Cohabiting relatives carry the duty; others may report.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of ordinary certificates; unnatural deaths go to the prosecutor.

electronicRegistration.note: The death report is not among the reports that may be filed electronically; the register itself is electronic.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Family-relations register (가족관계등록부, National Court Administration) and resident registration (주민등록)
centralPopulationRegister.note: The family register is national and electronic; the death report also cancels the resident registration.

governmentPropagation.note: The death report cancels the resident registration and is shared with the National Pension Service and NHIS; heirs can also use the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service to query assets and debts.

certificateAccess.note: Self, spouse and lineal blood relatives; others for state duties, litigation, statutory requirements or a legitimate interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: No general route for banks or insurers to check deaths; financial institutions are queried only when heirs use the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service via the FSS.

gaps: www.gov.kr, gov.kr, www.mois.go.kr, mois.go.kr and www.fss.or.kr were refused by the egress proxy; the Safe Inheritance One-stop Service is sourced from the MOIS Established Rule (행정안전부예규 제329호) on law.go.kr instead of the service pages.
The FSS 상속인 금융거래 조회 service rules (and any rule that the queried institution must freeze or flag accounts) could not be read.
No statutory feed of death reports to Statistics Korea (통계청) was found in the Act or the Supreme Court Rules; the vital-statistics route is not recorded.
Electoral roll: the roll is compiled from resident registration for each election (공직선거법), so a cancelled registration drops out, but no explicit death provision was quoted.
No doctor's duty to report abnormal deaths to the police (as in Japan's 医師法 art. 21) was found in 의료법; not recorded.
Passport (여권법) and driving-licence lapse on death were not read (law.go.kr fetch for 여권법 timed out).
Whether the cremation report requires a filed death report (장사법 시행규칙) was not checked.
